headline: Govt renames 5 Coast Guard ships, removing names of 4 national leaders
summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs has approved the renaming of vessels including those named after the four national leaders and 'Joy Bangla'.
details: The Bangladesh government has changed the names of five Bangladesh Coast Guard ships. This includes four vessels previously named after the four national leaders and one named 'Joy Bangla'.

According to a letter from the Ministry of Home Affairs' Border-3 branch sent to the Director General of the Coast Guard on Thursday, the changes were approved based on a proposal from the Coast Guard.
The ship 'BCGS Joy Bangla' (PC 208) has been renamed 'BCGS Adommo Bangla'.
The ship 'BCGS Syed Nazrul' (PL 71) is now 'BCGS Firoz Kabir', and 'BCGS Tajuddin' (PL 72) has become 'BCGS Nurul Islam'.
The ship 'BCGS gái Ngân' (PL 73) 'BCGS Mansur Ali' has been renamed 'BCGS M Hafizur Kabir', and 'BCGS Kamruzzaman' (PL 74) has become 'BCGS Ashraf Siddiqui'.
Coast Guard sources say the four new names are of Bangladesh Navy officers who were martyred while conducting operations both at home and in Bangladesh's territorial waters.

headline: 1,276 deaths from measles symptoms since March 15
summary: Four more people died in the last 24 hours, with Dhaka Division recording the highest number of fatalities overall.
details: Four people with measles symptoms died in the past 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS). All four deaths occurred in the Dhaka Division.
This brings the total death toll to 1,276 since March 15, with 1,171 deaths linked to measles symptoms and 105 confirmed measles deaths.
Dhaka Division has been the worst hit, recording 526 deaths. Sylhet follows with 204, Chattogram with 114, and Rajshahi with 93.
In the last 24 hours, 1,239 people nationwide developed measles symptoms, and 75 tested positive for the disease.
A total of 1,128 patients with measles symptoms were admitted to hospitals across the country during this period, with 387 in Dhaka Division.
Since March 15, 236,714 people have developed measles symptoms, and the disease has been confirmed in 24,294 cases.
The DGHS noted that the actual number of infections may be higher as not all patients, especially those outside hospitals, are tested.
Between March 15 and Thursday, 210,982 patients with measles symptoms were admitted to hospitals, and 202,394 of them have recovered.
